# CosmoEdge 1.2.0 — Release preparation in progress

[简体中文发布说明](v1.2.0.zh-CN.md)

This draft summarizes current source changes planned for 1.2.0 for review before
publication. The current public stable release remains **v1.1.0**, and the security
maintenance line remains **1.1.x**. The release date, package details, and 1.2.0
candidate acceptance results will be added when release preparation is complete.

## Main changes

- **Camera access and management APIs**: ONVIF discovery, manual registration,
  authentication, and video Profile selection; GB28181 registration, catalog queries,
  and playback with independently selectable TCP/UDP signaling and video transport.
  ONVIF currently excludes PTZ, audio, event subscriptions, and recording searches;
  GB28181 implements a SIP subset for directly connected devices, with compatibility
  still requiring validation in each deployment. Management v1 supports versioned
  model, scene, channel, schedule, and task delivery, resumable uploads, content
  deduplication, operation recovery, explicit start/stop, and status readback. See
  [ONVIF Access](../../docs/en/guide/onvif-access.md),
  [GB28181 Access](../../docs/en/guide/gb28181-access.md), and the
  [Management API](../../docs/en/reference/management.md).
- **Laya-V, YOLO26, and OBB**: Native BM1688 Laya-V integration adds alarm review,
  multiple questions per image/video ROI, persisted results, and model-name overlays.
  YOLO26 raw-output and oriented-box decoding, geometry propagation, and model
  templates are also included in source. A template does not establish that matching
  weights are installed or that every platform can run the model. See the
  [Model Reference](../../docs/en/reference/models.md) for model and platform requirements.
- **Console layout and themes**: Updated management pages, channel tasks, event
  details, live views, and flow-editor layouts, with persistent light, dark, and system
  appearance settings, a classic blue color scheme, and live overlay diagnostics.
- **Alarm-image privacy and output linkage**: Opt-in masking processes new alarm
  scene images and target crops before encoding, storage, and delivery. Missing
  required detection evidence or processing failures preserve the event while
  withholding affected images. Preview, recordings, historical images, images sent to
  external VLM services, and library enrollment images are outside this scope. Output
  linkage provides logical channels and hold times; repeated alarms on the same
  channel extend the hold until reset. Physical output requires board GPIO mapping,
  initialization, and write access. See [Configuration](../../docs/en/guide/configuration.md).
- **Alarm records and annotations**: Detection, face/body, and vehicle alarm records can
  be deleted individually or by current-page selection, with associated media cleanup;
  events still being recorded are protected. Alarm targets show class labels and measured
  confidence in preview and event views.
- **Image workflows and comparisons**: Image workflows without region configuration,
  structured business results, target and library match details, face/workwear library
  identification, and pair comparison. Each side of a pair must contain exactly one
  valid target; the result can be a 0–100 similarity score or a threshold decision.
  Scores are not identity probabilities or probabilities of matching workwear styles.
  Matching model weights are required. See [Image Analysis](../../docs/en/guide/image-analysis.md)
  and the [Image Detection API](../../docs/en/reference/image-detection-api.md).
- **Main fixes**: Preserved typed VLM results and timing in image/video events; repaired
  model initialization retries, task failure status, recovery after camera changes,
  library selection, model filtering, preset-model names, and the default confidence shown
  in task configuration. Other fixes cover active-log export snapshots, Sophon RGB
  normalization, YOLO NMS, GB28181 H.265 multi-slice preview and frame rates, media and
  recording handling, log retention, database read/write isolation, and task lifecycles. See the
  [Changelog](../../CHANGELOG.md#unreleased) for the full list.

## Platform scope and feature boundaries

1.2.0 plans to retain the existing platform scope. This release run will check all four
chip packages, with device installation, upgrade, and rollback validation limited to
BM1688; target-device results for the other chips are not part of this run. Final
deliverables and candidate results remain pending. Each build selects one
inference backend, and models and packages must match the target platform.

| Platform | Continuing path | Feature boundaries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sophon BM1688 | BMRT with chip-specific `.nn` models | The new native Laya-V path currently targets BM1688; each VLM still requires its matching model and runtime. |
| Sophon CV186X | BMRT with chip-specific `.nn` models and VLM support | Complete BM1688 packages cannot be reused; BM1688 Laya-V support does not establish CV186X support. |
| Rockchip RK3576 | RKNN, MPP/RGA, and RKLLM VLM support | Models and media runtimes are target-specific; the protected RKNN model extension in source does not establish RV1126B support. |
| Rockchip RV1126B | Separate RKNN and MPP/RGA path | RKLLM is excluded and VLM support is not claimed; community example models retain their own manifests and licenses. |
| x86 Linux / Windows | ONNX Runtime CPU, Docker Compose, and persistent named volumes | A development runtime; device installation packages and NPU performance are not promised. |
| Apple Silicon macOS | Isolated Docker Preview | A single-local-video workflow under `linux/amd64` emulation, not native arm64 performance. |

Open/Protected model distribution and authorization remain separate concerns. See the
[Build Guide](../../docs/en/guide/build.md) and
[macOS Docker Preview](../../docs/en/guide/macos-docker-preview.md). Existing v1.1
performance reports describe only their recorded candidates and workloads; they do not
establish acceptance for 1.2.0, new models, or new features.

## Upgrade considerations from 1.1.0

- **Match the chip and distribution profile**: Once final packages exist, select
  packages and models for the device chip and Open/Protected profile, and check
  `TARGET_CHIP`, checksums, and required authorization. BM1688, CV186X, RK3576, and
  RV1126B packages are not interchangeable.
- **Back up data**: Stop the service, back up the actual persistent data to a separate
  filesystem, and verify that the backup is readable. Retain custom models, resources,
  and authorization material separately. Keep the old package and backups until the
  upgraded service and business workflows have been verified. See the
  [Deployment Guide](../../docs/en/guide/deployment.md) for backup and installation
  procedures; its existing 1.0.0 → 1.1.0 records do not establish acceptance for
  1.1.0 → 1.2.0.
- **Device resource overwrite rules**: By default, old `resource` content absent from
  the new package is retained, while package files replace old files at the same path.
  Back up custom templates or models that share those paths. `CLEAN_RESOURCE=1` instead
  uses only packaged resources and must not be treated as preserving existing resources.
- **Retain x86 volumes**: Keep both the user-data and application-resource volumes;
  do not run `docker compose down -v`. Updating the image alone does not refresh an
  existing application-resource volume. Back it up and check the templates and model
  resources required by the new version.

## Maintenance plan and pending information

The plan is to **maintain only 1.2.x after the formal 1.2.0 release**, ending 1.1.x
maintenance at that point. Until publication, the current public stable and security
maintenance line remains 1.1.x as described in [SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md).

Before publication, add the release date, approved source revision, exact package
filenames and checksums for each target, and verification results and known limitations
bound to the final candidates. This draft contains no package details that have not
been generated and no acceptance conclusions for checks that have not been performed.
